scenarios.name: Credential access
scenarios.description: Tries the common ways an attacker with admin rights pulls credentials off a Windows machine: LSASS memory dumps, registry hive copies, and enabling plaintext credential caching. Exercises LSA protection, Credential Guard, and Defender.

scenarios.name: UAC bypass
scenarios.description: Registry-hijack UAC bypasses (fodhelper, Event Viewer) and switching UAC off. Exercises UAC configuration and detection of auto-elevation abuse.

scenarios.name: Persistence
scenarios.description: Run keys, scheduled tasks, new local (admin) accounts, and service hijacking — the ways malware survives a reboot.

scenarios.name: Execution and defense evasion
scenarios.description: Encoded/fileless PowerShell, offensive cmdlet names, turning off PowerShell logging and RDP NLA, and rundll32 script proxy execution. Exercises AMSI, logging, and detection coverage.

scenarios.name: Local discovery
scenarios.description: The reconnaissance an intruder runs first: accounts, groups, system and network configuration, firewall rules, processes. All benign; mostly a test of whether it is logged.
